content.title: About
content.content: Fried eggplant consists of sliced eggplant that is deep‑fried until golden and crisp. The flesh is soft and mildly sweet, while the frying gives it a crunchy texture and rich aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggplant belongs to the nightshade family and is a relative of tomatoes and potatoes.
It is called “aubergine” in British English, “eggplant” in American English, and “brinjal” in South Asia.
The deep purple color comes from anthocyanins, which have antioxidant properties.
Eggplant is a staple in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Asian cuisines.
In many countries fried eggplant is served as a bar snack or in salads.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: When eaten in moderation, fried eggplant can fit into a calorie‑controlled diet.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: High fat content from frying
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories and saturated fat, which should be limited.

items.title: Nightshade allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggplant.

items.title: Salt and seasoning
items.content: Excessive salt can increase the risk of hypertension.

items.title: Tough skin
items.content: The skin can be hard to digest for people with gastrointestinal issues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried eggplant is served hot as an appetizer, in salads, sandwiches, or as a side dish with meat. It pairs well with fresh herbs, lemon juice, or a yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fried eggplant in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags; it will retain flavor for up to 2 months.
